name: Account Takeover
description: Criminals gain control of customer accounts through phishing, credential stuffing, SIM swap or malware, then change details and extract funds. Early detection relies on login, device and change-of-details signals.

sources.text: UK Finance, Annual Fraud Report (specify year, e.g. 2025)
FinCEN, Advisory to Financial Institutions on Cyber-Events and Cyber-Enabled Crime (FIN-2016-A005, 2016)
FFIEC, Authentication and Access to Financial Institution Services and Systems (2021)

exposure.rationale: Credential/device compromise in digital and call-centre channels.

indicators.name: Login from new device, country or emulator
indicators.canon: Login from unfamiliar device, location or infrastructure
indicators.desc: Session originates from a device, country, emulator or network not previously associated with the customer, including shortly after a phishing event.
indicators.ctx: Session originates from unfamiliar infrastructure, possibly using an emulator or anonymising proxy.
refs: UK Finance, Annual Fraud Report (published annually)

indicators.name: Multiple failed logins followed by success
indicators.canon: Multiple failed logins followed by success
indicators.desc: Repeated failed authentication attempts, often across accounts from one source, followed by successful access.
indicators.ctx: Credential stuffing or brute force pattern preceding successful access.
refs: UK Finance, Annual Fraud Report (published annually)

indicators.name: Contact details or phone number changed then high-value payment
indicators.canon: Recent change of contact or delivery details
indicators.desc: Email, phone, address or statement delivery details are changed, especially shortly before unusual activity or redirecting mail to a third party.
indicators.ctx: Email, phone or address updated minutes before outbound transactions.
refs: UK Finance, Annual Fraud Report (published annually)

indicators.name: SIM swap or number port detected
indicators.canon: SIM swap or number port before transfers
indicators.desc: Mobile number is ported or SIM replaced shortly before one-time-passcode-protected actions or outbound transfers.
indicators.ctx: Telecom signals show recent SIM change before OTP-protected actions.
refs: UK Finance, Annual Fraud Report (published annually)

indicators.name: New payee added and funds drained rapidly
indicators.canon: New payee added and funds drained rapidly
indicators.desc: Attacker adds beneficiaries and transfers most of the balance in one session.
indicators.ctx: Attacker adds beneficiaries and transfers most of the balance in one session.
refs: UK Finance, Annual Fraud Report (published annually)

indicators.name: Password reset or credential change from unrecognised channel
indicators.canon: Password reset or credential change from unrecognised channel
indicators.desc: Self-service reset triggered from an unfamiliar environment.
indicators.ctx: Self-service reset triggered from an unfamiliar environment.
refs: UK Finance, Annual Fraud Report (published annually)

indicators.name: Card replacement or wallet provisioning to new address
indicators.canon: Card replacement or wallet provisioning to new address
indicators.desc: Attacker requests cards or tokens to alternate addresses.
indicators.ctx: Attacker requests cards or tokens to alternate addresses.
refs: UK Finance, Annual Fraud Report (published annually)

indicators.name: Mule accounts receiving compromised funds
indicators.canon: Account receiving funds from multiple apparent fraud victims
indicators.desc: A new or low-activity account receives payments from several unrelated individuals who appear to be victims of fraud or phishing, followed by onward movement or cash-out.
refs: UK Finance, Annual Fraud Report (published annually)

indicators.name: Session shows automated or scripted interaction
indicators.canon: Session shows automated or scripted interaction
indicators.desc: Non-human timing, headless browser or scripted API calls.
indicators.ctx: Non-human timing, headless browser or scripted API calls.
refs: UK Finance, Annual Fraud Report (published annually)
